title: COVID-19 rules made 2020 USA-NPN volunteer spring plant dates about 5 days late, mainly at partner-group sites, but not German or Swiss station records or US camera dates (2010-2025)
abstract: Question: a campaign publication found a +16 day artifact in 2020 UK butterfly first dates. Do other phenology networks have a 2020 artifact? Data: DWD annual reporters (Germany, 7 wild plants, 2,898 stations, 1995-2023), MeteoSwiss phenology (175 stations, 1995-2025), USA-NPN Nature's Notebook first-yes dates (12 woody species, 11,100 plants, 2010-2024) and PhenoCam V3 deciduous camera dates (58 eastern US sites). Method: a plan written before the models; station fixed effects, local temperature and a linear year term fitted without one held-out year; the 2020 spring group mean compared with the other held-out years; rule |z| >= 2 and >= 3 days. Results: USA-NPN spring dates were +5.1 days late in 2020 (65 species-phenophases, z = 3.4, latest of 13 years, other years -2.7 to +1.7; 2021 -0.7). Records fell by 32% while sites did not fall. At partner-group sites (schools, nature centres, parks) the share of onsets with a 'no' record within 7 days fell from 64% to 41%; at other sites it did not change. With only these precise onsets the 2020 anomaly fell to +3.1 days (z = 1.1). Post hoc, May phases were +7.7 days (z = 4.2) and February-March phases were not late. DWD (-2.8 days, z = -1.5) and MeteoSwiss (-2.2 days, z = -1.4) were early, not late, with no change in station counts; PhenoCam was +0.3 days (z = 0.2). An exploratory urban-minus-rural contrast in Germany gave no 2020 signal (-0.8 days, z = -1.0). Conclusion: the artifact follows observer conditions; USA-NPN 2020 spring records need exclusion or a visit-precision filter; German, Swiss and camera records do not. Limitations: one temperature model per network; the NPN result needs the winter term (tmax_spring only: +3.8 days, z = 1.7); 12 NPN species; few cameras in 2020.
